case: Baseline architecture evaluation: Modular monolith vs microservices for RepoRisk

jurors.name: Dr. Aris Thorne
jurors.perspective: Evaluates parser bugs, AST traversal edge cases, SAST accuracy, injection vulnerabilities, and deterministic vs speculative findings.
jurors.bias: Extreme skepticism toward unvalidated scanner claims and regex-based AST approximations.

jurors.name: Marcus Vance
jurors.perspective: Evaluates container sandboxing, subprocess execution boundaries, memory limits, timeouts, disk quotas, and blast radius isolation.
jurors.bias: Treats all analyzed code as actively hostile and demands rigorous execution barriers.

jurors.name: Liam O'Connor
jurors.perspective: Ponytail advocate. Checks whether proposed abstractions are necessary, evaluates standard library usage, YAGNI adherence, and maintenance burden.
jurors.bias: Rejects bloated dependencies, unnecessary microservices, and premature architectural complexity.

briefs.prosecution: Microservices introduce immense operational friction, network failure modes, RPC overhead, and complex deployment requirements prematurely.
briefs.defense: A modular monolith offers strong compile-time type boundaries, zero-network in-process communication, straightforward local testing, and deterministic deployment.

arch_minimalist.rationale: NOT GUILTY. Monolith is strictly aligned with YAGNI and minimalist principles.

sec_appsec.rationale: NOT GUILTY. In-process boundary eliminates network MITM and unauthenticated internal RPC endpoints.

devops_sre.rationale: NOT GUILTY. Greatly simplifies container sandboxing and local developer replication.

verdict.summary: The modular monolith is unanimously upheld as the required architecture for RepoRisk.
